exact_claim: A 22.05 kHz vs 16.00 kHz sample-rate mismatch in legacy evaluation pipelines inflated Word Error Rate by ~3% absolute (493 word errors) on dev_assessment without any acoustic model change.
evaluation_protocol: Legacy raw-array passing vs Kaiser windowed sinc 16 kHz resampler
reproduced_value: Historical: 27.39% WER (4,614 errors) -> Corrected: 24.46% WER (4,121 errors); Delta = -493 errors
notes: 100% of eliminated errors (493) belong to the 431 Bolbosh 22.05 kHz files; 570 16 kHz files produced identical predictions.

exact_claim: Acoustic foundation model B-02C was trained with active dynamic resampling to 16,000 Hz, preserving physically uncorrupted speech representations.
evaluation_protocol: Source inspection & signal tracing across representative audio inputs
reproduced_value: torchaudio.transforms.Resample(orig_sr, 16000) active during all Stage 9 training
notes: Internal representations of B-02C were never exposed to unresampled temporal dilation.

exact_claim: On canonical 16 kHz evaluation, Stage 15 E-03 and Stage 9 B-02C are statistically indistinguishable, differing by exactly 1 word error across 16,845 reference words.
evaluation_protocol: EduCasheer-Kashmiri-ASR-Eval-v2 (Kaiser sinc 16k, KenLM alpha=0.35, beta=-0.50, beam=16)
notes: Prior claims that MWER provided major gains were artifacts of evaluating on unresampled audio.

exact_claim: Reducing KenLM beam search width from 16 to 8 with prune_history=False caused an artificial 84-word error penalty in Stage 20T, which is eliminated by restoring beam width 16.
reproduced_value: Beam 8: 24.85% WER (4,186 errors) -> Beam 16: 24.46% WER (4,121 errors); Delta = -65 to -84 errors
notes: Achieves 100.0% exact string match (1,001/1,001 utts) with canonical benchmark.

exact_claim: Tuning language model parameters (alpha=0.20, beta=-0.50) on calibration speech reduces dev_assessment errors from 4,121 to 4,089 (24.27% WER) without retraining neural weights.
evaluation_protocol: Grid search on dev_calibration followed by locked evaluation on dev_assessment
notes: Gains are small (28-32 words out of 16,845; bootstrap p=0.0847, paired t-test p=0.317); dev_assessment was examined during study.

exact_claim: The 16-best candidate beam oracle WER ceiling is 19.23% (3,240 errors), demonstrating that 881 word errors (21.4% of total errors) are recoverable by hypothesis rescoring.
evaluation_protocol: Minimum Levenshtein distance hypothesis extraction across N-best candidate list
reproduced_value: N=1: 24.46% (4,121 errors) -> N=16: 19.23% (3,240 errors); Recoverable = 881 errors
notes: 84.5% of errors (3,240) remain out-of-beam acoustic deficiencies requiring acoustic scaling or dialect modeling.

exact_claim: Acoustic training scaling from 92.9h (B-01) to 165.3h (B-02C) yields a statistically significant 6.02% absolute WER reduction (33.86% to 27.84% greedy WER; p < 0.0001) on the 6,728-sample validation split.
evaluation_protocol: Standardized greedy CTC decoding on val.jsonl with 10,000 bootstrap resamples
notes: Speaker-disjoint validation set; highly statistically significant scaling effect.

exact_claim: Zero-shot foundation models (Whisper-Large-v3, Whisper-Medium) fail catastrophically on Kashmiri speech with WERs exceeding 84% due to absence of native Kashmiri language tokens and diacritic modeling.
evaluation_protocol: Zero-shot Whisper decoding with language forced or auto-detected
reproduced_value: Whisper-Large-v3: 84.12% WER; Whisper-Medium: 88.65% WER; Whisper-Small: 107.06% WER
notes: Causes severe cross-lingual hallucination loops into Slavic or Devanagari Hindi text.
